description:
🚀 NASA Space Apps Challenge

We are a multidisciplinary team from Peru participating in NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. Our project focuses on developing an AI-powered interactive platform integrating NASA datasets, geospatial analysis, and geological information to identify and evaluate lunar and Martian terrain analogs, including sites in Peru. Our goal is to support safer, more efficient space exploration through scientific analysis, engineering solutions, and data-driven decision-making.
summary: We are developing an interactive geospatial prototype to identify and compare potential terrestrial analog sites in Peru with lunar and Martian environments. Using open geologic and terrain data, we document similarities, limitations, and possible uses for rover mobility and habitat planning. Our pilot examines La Joya, Arequipa, with traceable sources and candidate polygons.
details:
Problem: Terrestrial environments can support lunar and Martian exploration, but visual resemblance alone cannot establish a useful analog.
Solution: We propose a geospatial viewer that records candidate coordinates and polygons in Peru and organizes evidence on terrain, lithology, and exploration-relevant conditions.
Pilot: La Joya, Arequipa. A preliminary GEOCATMIN query identified the Millo Formation (Np-mi3), including conglomerates and tuffs, in an inspected map unit; its exact spatial correspondence with the pilot point and its mineralogy remain to be verified.
Method: (1) select a location; (2) draw a polygon; (3) assess slopes and terrain; (4) query terrestrial geology; (5) link identifiable lunar or Martian data products; (6) explain analogies, differences, and limitations.
Value: A reproducible workflow, traceable data, and potential use cases for rover mobility and preliminary habitat planning.
Status: Prototype and analysis in progress; no claim of construction suitability or proven mineralogical equivalence.
